appendix.title: Relation to BSF4ooRexx and the Sister Bridges
appendix.para: The bridge was asked for by Rony G. Flatscher, the author of BSF4ooRexx, the bridge between ooRexx and Java, and follows its conventions where .NET allows it: .NET arrays as Rexx Arrays from 1, as BSF_ARRAY_REFERENCE; enum values as objects; box and unbox with its indicators; the RexxObject methods SendMessage ... SendMessage5 and SendMessageScope, as RexxProxy's; the prefixes of the standard streams; and the event thread's classes, from BSF.CLS.

appendix.para: The sister bridges. ooRexx/WASM's JSObject (ooRexx in the browser) and ooRexx/Python share the shape: one entry object (&net; as .js and .py), proxies by reference, names in any case with an exact form, handlers with the same queued model, and Rexx classes that extend classes of the other side. ooRexx/.NET departs from them where .NET differs: names are caseless with the member that starts in uppercase winning (.NET's convention; .js prefers lowercase), an unknown member is an error rather than .js~undefined, and the exact access and introspection are methods of &net; rather than of the proxies, because [] is .NET's indexer and Invoke one of .NET's commonest member names. The design notes mark every such difference with Δ.
